title: Quick Infer Handoff Playbook — Pricing & Dev Onramp Notes
content:
TL;DR:
A compact playbook for handing an engineer from curiosity -> first useful inference in ~5 minutes, with three pricing-language variations to test in-run onboarding microcopy. Goal: reduce time-to-first-meaningful-call, limit surprise billing, and create predictable upgrade triggers (credits -> pay-as-you-go -> reserved).

Audience & problem: 
- Primary audience: backend/frontend engineers, ML engineers integrating generation/embeddings into product flows.
- Pain: friction in getting reliable latency/cost estimates, unclear unit economics, and unclear upgrade threshold (when to move from free credits to committed capacity).

High-level positioning lines (test as A/B copy):
- Engineer-facing (short): "Start generating in minutes. Predictable latency, transparent token costs."
- Product PM-facing (short): "Ship LLM features with confident performance and clear economics."
- Ops/security (short): "Hosted inference with enterprise-grade auditability and escape hatches to Dedicated/Private."

Developer-first value props (ranked):
1) Predictable performance: per-route token breakdowns and latency SLOs so engineers can plan UX budgets.
2) Transparent unit pricing: clear per-token units + per-request baseline for small prompt-heavy workloads.
3) Quick SDKs and sample apps: copy-paste curl, Python, and Node snippets that “just work”.
4) Seamless upgrade path: free credits -> PAYG with soft caps -> reserved commits for scale.
5) Fallbacks and graceful degradation: automatic routing to cheaper model variants under capacity constraints with telemetry surfaced.

Quickstart flows (3 canonical paths to instrument in product/text):
1) 3-line curl (onboarding copy):
- Microcopy: "One curl. Two seconds. First token visible."
- Steps: create key (free credits), curl example to /v1/generate with short prompt, show streaming chunk.
- Success metric: developer sees first token stream < 3s.

2) Python SDK (most common):
- Code snippet (minimal): import rdw; rdw.Client(api_key).generate(prompt=..).stream()
- Playbook: include sample app that stores trace id and shows cost estimate per call (ui overlay).
- Metric: sample app deployed to internal sandbox in < 10m.

3) Embed-in-playground + onboarding checklist (non-blocking):
- Playground computes estimated tokens + cost before call, shows expected latency percentile.
- Prompt templates for common use cases: summarize, classify, search-augment, chat.
- Metric: 35% of new accounts run a saved playground template.

Pricing-language experiments (3 variants to test in onboarding microcopy):
Variant A: "Engineer clarity" (precise)
- "Free credits for 14 days. Then pay-as-you-go: $0.0007 per generation-token, $0.0004 per embedding-unit. Estimated call cost shown before you send. Soft daily cap to prevent surprises."

Variant B: "Value-first" (product-focused)
- "Start for free and pay only for what you use — optimized autoscaling and caching reduce your per-call spend by up to 5x vs unmanaged endpoints. Reserved plans available for predictable throughput."

Variant C: "Simplicity" (minimal friction)
- "Free trial. Simple metering, single monthly bill. Upgrade when you need guaranteed capacity."

Pricing UX mechanics to include in flows: 
- Preflight estimator: show estimated tokens and price before send.
- Soft caps & auto-notify: default account limit that prompts upgrade email/in-app after threshold.
- Cost breakouts in logs: per-request token count + model variant used.
- Credits expiry messaging: clear date and how to convert into committed spend.

Competitive analysis notes (quick bullets — needs validation):
- Public cloud endpoints (AWS/GCP): strong for enterprise procurement but slow in developer time-to-first-call; pricing units often opaque across layers (VM + managed service). Redwood edge: unified token pricing + sample UX lowers lift.
- LLM API incumbents (A, B): very easy to try; some lock-in via proprietary model variants. Redwood advantage: curated open-models + explicit fallback policies and escape hatches to self-hosted Private.
- Inference infra vendors (X, Y): great for on-prem performance but heavy ops. Redwood advantage: hosted that mirrors Dedicated/Private configs so migration path is straightforward.

Top messaging tests to run (hypotheses):
- H1: Engineer-facing precise pricing reduces billing-related churn by 20% in first 30 days.
- H2: Showing estimated cost preflight increases conversion from trial->payg by 12%.
- H3: Offering a "playground save" with recorded token+cost history increases retention of non-engineer PM users.

Microcopy snippets (for product UI & emails):
- Console header: "Make a test call — we’ll estimate the cost before you send."
- Billing tooltip: "Token pricing varies by model; we’ll show a per-call estimate and optional soft cap."
- Upgrade email subject: "You’re nearing your free credits — keep building with predictable pricing."

Measurement & instrumentation checklist (what PM/RD should track):
- Time-to-first-token (median+90p) from account creation.
- % of accounts that run estimator before sending first call.
- Trial->PAYG conversion, broken down by whether estimator was used.
- Incidents of billing surprise support tickets per 1k trials.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: showing precise per-token cost discourages experimentation. Mitigation: show both absolute and relative estimates and propose a sample budget ("try 5 free experiments" short-run credit).
- Risk: too many upgrade prompts -> fatigue. Mitigation: a single soft-cap nudge + weekly summary.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (tickets to spin up):
- Decide default soft cap value (JIRA candidate).
- Define precise language for embeddings billing (per-item vs per-unit).
- Create 3 A/B variants for preflight estimator UI (mockups from design needed).
- Instrument quickstart sample apps to emit a telemetry tag so we can measure time-to-first-token.

Next steps (short-term roadmap):
- Week 0–1: implement estimator on playground + preflight copy variant A and measure. Owner: Ellen.
- Week 1–3: run A/B on pricing language (A vs C). Owner: Diego.
- Week 3–6: create SDK example with cost overlay + launch email flow. Owner: Samir.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep microcopy short; engineers skip fluff. But provide one sentence of reassurance about billing safety.
- Avoid words like "cheap" in public-facing pricing. Use "optimized" / "cost-effective".
- Reach out to Applied ML for realistic per-call token baselines for common templates.

Appendix: sample quickstart copy (one-paragraph):
"Create an API key and try a sample request in under 2 minutes. Our SDK shows estimated tokens and cost before you invoke, and streams the first token in <3s on average. Start with free credits, set a soft daily cap, and upgrade to pay-as-you-go when you need sustained throughput."

— end of playbook draft —

Feedback wanted: prioritize which pricing variant to test first and default soft cap suggestion (low/medium/high).
